## kb_to_source
- Every normative sentence in the 11 EWC/ERD documents and the base documents above maps to a source atom. The only additions are worked examples, boundary tables and Q&A, all derivations from the source.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each tool name appears only in its own hub. Checked across all 60 docs plus every other product's docs.
- Opening world state written in as a policy fact: none. A search for task names, SKUs, prices, initials and customers across the corpus found nothing.
- Additions or rewrites: none in the EWC/ERD documents beyond D1, which is an omission.
- made_to_order_deposit_payment "Scope notes" restates the remake's own charge timing ("Its deposit is charged when the remake is taken") in another policy's document. This is faithful to the ERD rule and states no dependency. No finding.

### Differences
- **D1 (omission, EWC assembly).** The source sentence that puts the work share, the personalisation multiplier and the three reliefs into one product, with the cap at the deposit held and the rounding applied to that whole product, is not carried. Visible text:
  - made_to_order_work_charge: "The work charge is worked out as one product of the reserved price (unit price times units) and the work share … The cap at the deposit held and the rounding to the cent apply to that product. The amount kept is therefore the lower of that product and the deposit held".
  - footwear_client_relief: "multiplies the work charge by the band the count falls in".
  - return_record_relief: "The count multiplies the work charge".
  - rewards_tenure_relief: "Marlowe Rewards tenure relief multiplies the work charge".

  None of the three relief documents states when its multiplier applies relative to the cap, although the source fixes that moment. In this task the cap binds (243.00 > 151.20), so the reading "cap, then reliefs" gives 79.29/71.91 against the source's 127.43/23.77. Affected: made_to_order_work_charge ("How the figure is put together"), footwear_client_relief, return_record_relief and rewards_tenure_relief (each "Rule"/"Relief" paragraph).

### dependency_form (revision 2)
**New finding E1 — KB-EXPLICIT RED (low severity; semantics correct, scored values unaffected).**
- The rewritten computation document made_to_order_work_charge ("How the figure is put together") now reads: "The work charge is worked out as one product, **starting from** the reserved price (unit price times units) multiplied by the work share … The cap … are the last steps. They apply to the **finished product** as a whole, **never to a part of it**."
- Meaning: price × work share is where the product *starts*. The "finished product" differs from it and has "parts" that the cap must not touch.
- To a reader holding only the computation document, this says that further multiplicands join the baseline product. That is a hint that something modifies the baseline, which the discrete topology forbids in a computation document. The relief and personalisation documents now carry the cap moment themselves.
- Round 1 had no such wording ("one product of the reserved price … and the work share … apply to that product"). E1 was introduced by the D1 fix.
- Location: made_to_order_work_charge, paragraph "How the figure is put together", first three sentences.

Everything else is unchanged from round 1 and passes: the prerequisite sentence form, tool names, titles, factor documents and blind hop marks. The factor documents' references to "the same product … before the cap" carry the source's pinned cap moment (a required atom), not a pointer.
**KB-EXPLICIT RED (E1).**
